title: Let's Make a Trading Card Game 24: Complexity in TCGs
summary: The video explores strategies to make trading card games more accessible to new players, focusing on the game Multiverse Cosmic Conquest. The speaker, Leandro, discusses various methods to simplify the learning process, such as tutorials and preconstructed decks, while also providing updates on the game's development and the challenges of balancing simplicity and complexity in game design.

points.main_point: The speaker discusses the complexity inherent in trading card games (TCGs) and the challenges it poses for new players.
points.explanation: The speaker explains that TCGs are generally complex due to their rules and the vast number of choices in deck building. This complexity creates a barrier for new players who may not understand the genre or the rules. The speaker suggests that new players often learn the game through explanations from experienced players, but this is not always reliable, especially for new games where all players are new. The speaker also mentions that some TCGs use base sets with simpler cards to help new players, but this does not eliminate the complexity of deck building.

points.main_point: The speaker outlines various strategies to reduce the complexity and barrier of entry for new players in TCGs.
points.explanation: The speaker discusses several methods to make TCGs more accessible to new players. These include using base sets with simpler cards, creating preconstructed decks that are easy to understand, and dividing the game into different modes with varying levels of complexity. The speaker also mentions that online TCGs can utilize in-game tutorials to teach players the basics of the game. Additionally, the speaker suggests that having a friend explain the rules is still one of the best ways to learn a TCG.

points.main_point: The speaker provides updates on the development of Multiverse Cosmic Conquest, including art progress, playtesting, and programming efforts.
points.explanation: The speaker mentions that concept art for the races and vehicles in Multiverse Cosmic Conquest has been created, and artists have started working on the artwork for the Arsenal cards. Playtesting has been ongoing, with smaller iterations focusing on adjustments to power stats, health stats, and card costs. The speaker also discusses the creation of a tutorial series to explain the rules of the game and the development of a rulebook that includes sections on multiplayer games. Additionally, the speaker talks about the high-level design for the online version of the game and the costs associated with its development.

points.main_point: The speaker states that the Kickstarter campaign for Multiverse Cosmic Conquest will start on September 15th, 2017, and the series will continue to be released weekly until the game is released.
points.explanation: The speaker announces that the Kickstarter campaign for Multiverse Cosmic Conquest will begin on September 15th, 2017, and if everything goes as planned, it will end on October 15th. The speaker also mentions that the Let's Make a Trading Card Game series will be released weekly on Saturdays, even after the Kickstarter campaign ends. The speaker emphasizes that the series will continue to be released regularly until the game is released.

points.main_point: The speaker suggests several strategies to lower the complexity barrier for new players in trading card games.
points.explanation: The speaker suggests using tutorials, preconstructed decks, and simplifying common cards to make the game more accessible. The speaker also mentions the importance of balancing the complexity of rules and cards to ensure the game remains interesting and manageable. The speaker highlights that Multiverse Cosmic Conquest will include a tutorial in the online version of the game, which will walk new players through their first few games with a preconstructed deck.
